name: Record Keeper Quartz
spiritual: Supports Third Eye and Crown focus
Offers a symbol for stored wisdom
physical: Crystal healers link it to mental stillness
Many people keep it nearby to support a quiet study space
summary: Record Keeper Quartz bears raised triangles on its faces and is a classic crystal-lore stone for stored wisdom, study, memory and deep meditation.
intro: A record keeper is a quartz crystal whose faces carry small, raised or recessed triangles, called trigons, pointing the same way and sitting neatly on one or more of the termination faces. They are real surface features, formed during growth or by gentle dissolution, and they can be so sharp that a fingertip can feel them. Many look like tiny etched pyramids or a tidy set of shallow dents. Most record keepers are clear or milky quartz points of modest size, and they are found in Brazil, Arkansas, Madagascar and other quartz-rich localities. The triangle is the whole point: a simple, crisp geometric mark that crystal lovers read as a built-in symbol.
history: Trigons on quartz faces were noted by mineralogists long before they were given metaphysical meaning, and they appear in crystallography diagrams as a sign of the mineral's trigonal symmetry. The name record keeper began to spread in the 1980s and 1990s through crystal-healing writers, such as those who wrote about the Akashic Records, a theosophical idea of a universal archive of every thought and event. Crystals with triangle marks were seen as keys to that archive. As this is a modern spiritual idea, there is no ancient folklore for the stone, but it has become a staple of contemporary crystal practice, and a favorite among diviners and meditators.
meaning: Practitioners call record keeper quartz a library card for the soul. The triangles are said to mark crystals that store and release knowledge, and are used in meditation to access memory, insight and the so-called Akashic Records. They are tied to the Third Eye, Crown and Soul Star chakras, and appear in study and divination practices. People often hold one while asking about patterns in their lives or the lessons of a past event. Some use it in writing and learning, picturing the triangle as a tiny door to understanding. Because it is a clear quartz, it is also considered to amplify whatever intention you set, so it responds to clear, specific questions.
howToUse: Hold a record keeper in your receiving hand and trace the triangle with your finger while you set a single clear question. Sit quietly for ten minutes, notice what comes, and write it down afterward. Place it on a bookshelf or study desk, or hold it during reading and research. Lie down with it on your forehead for a short Third Eye meditation. In a grid, use it at the center with clear quartz points directed inward. Many people also keep one near a journal or divination deck. A morning minute with the stone sets a thoughtful tone.
care: Quartz is hard and stable, so record keeper quartz can handle regular cleansing. A brief rinse in lukewarm water, a soft brush for dust in the trigons and a dry cloth keep it clear. Sunlight and moonlight are both safe. Smoke, sound and selenite plates are other good options. Avoid scrubbing hard, since the trigons are shallow marks and can fill with grime. Store in a soft pouch to protect the termination, and keep it away from harder gems that could scratch it.
identify: Genuine trigons are tiny, regular triangles, all pointing in the same direction on a single face, and they are part of the crystal rather than painted or etched lines. Under a loupe, the edges are sharp and glassy and sit at the crystal's natural angles. Carved or sandblasted imitations look uneven, with rounded or scattered marks. Be wary of glass or resin points with pressed triangles. Note that not every triangle-faced crystal is a record keeper; the marks should be crisp and raised or sunken, easily visible and consistently oriented.

faq.q: What is a record keeper crystal?
faq.a: It is a quartz crystal with raised or recessed triangles, called trigons, on its faces. Crystal lovers see these marks as symbols of stored wisdom and use the crystals for study, meditation and Akashic Records work.

Yes, genuine trigons are natural growth or dissolution features of quartz and follow the crystal's symmetry. They are crisp, uniform triangles pointing the same direction, unlike hand-carved or painted marks on imitations.

faq.q: How do I use a record keeper?
faq.a: Hold it while you meditate, trace the triangle with your finger and ask one clear question. Many people place it on a desk or bookshelf to support study, or on the forehead for a short Third Eye meditation.
